paragraphs: The Vario 512D is part of the lighter-chassis Vario range, produced from 1996 to 2013. It used two engines across its production run: the OM602, a 2.9-litre inline-five diesel, and the later OM611, a 2.2-litre inline-four diesel. Both are well-proven commercial diesel units shared with the equivalent-era Sprinter, and both share the same known wear pattern — timing chain and gear wear, and injector seal deterioration over time. The Vario range was discontinued in 2013, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every VARIO 512D on the road.

cards.body: A 2.9-litre inline-five diesel fitted to the Vario 512D from 1996 onwards. Known for injector seal and timing chain/gear wear — see the callout above. We replace timing chain components, timing gears, injector seals and gaskets as standard on every OM602 rebuild.

A 2.2-litre inline-four diesel fitted to the Vario 512D from the late 1990s onward, as a lighter alternative to the OM602. Known for the same injector seal and timing chain/gear wear pattern as the OM602 — see the callout above. We replace the same components as standard on every OM611 rebuild.
